why:
The absence code worth the most, and the one hardest to reach any other way. `concept` declares `supersedes` and no instance in this corpus authors it — the declaration exists for no other reason. A relationship a class licenses and nothing uses is either an ontology that reached past its corpus or a gap worth an open question, and from outside it looks exactly like a mistyped name: the class file says it exists, the gate has nothing to complain about, and the traversal returns zero rows either way. It is deliberately DISTINCT from `relationship-unknown`, which is the arm `concept -leads-to-> concept` reaches; the two come back identically and their repairs are opposite. `instances` is the denominator — how many nodes reached the step before the hop — because *none of four* and *none of nine hundred* are different facts about a corpus. 

`elsewhere` names `upstream` here, and this is the only case in this directory where it is non-empty — before the fixture gained an installed dependency (#333) the field was empty on every response, so a server that never looked passed identically to one that did. It is a POINTER and not an answer: the dependency holds `concept` instances, which is all that is claimed. Whether any of them authors `supersedes` is that corpus's business and is what `across: true` would go and ask.
